subject: Future Tech
title: The Rocket Equation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Rocket Equation.

hook.text: The hardest part of space travel is the first 100 kilometers. Escaping Earth's gravity demands enormous energy.

buildup.text: The Tsiolkovsky rocket equation shows that most of a rocket's mass must be fuel. Payload is a tiny sliver.

discovery.text: To reach orbit, a rocket must hit 28,000 km/h. The Saturn V burned 2,000 tons of fuel in the first 2.5 minutes.

twist.text: The equation is tyrannical. Adding one kilogram of payload requires several kilograms more fuel, which needs more fuel.

climax.text: Reusable rockets and orbital refueling are humanity's best tricks to cheat the equation and make space affordable.

punchline.text: Gravity is the tax on every kilogram we launch.

quiz.question: What does the Tsiolkovsky equation primarily describe?
options: The relationship between fuel mass and payload
